title: Translation and Literary Design of Matthew 5:13-16
caption: <bp-cite>Matthew 5:13-16</bp-cite>. Translation and Literary Design by Tim Mackie for BibleProject Classroom: The Messianic Torah (2024)
usx:
<usx version="2.6">
  <para>
    <group title="Salt" type="primary">
      <group>
        <verse number="13" /> <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="red">Y’all</char> are <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="orange">the salt</char> <char mark-variant="text" mark-color="orange">of the land</char>. 
      </group>
      <optbreak />
      <group>
        But if <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="orange">the salt</char> loses flavor/is foolish, 
      </group>
      <group indent="1">
        with what can it be <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="orange">made salty</char> again? 
      </group>
      <optbreak />
      <group>
        It’s useful for <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="turquoise" word-lang="greek" word-original="οὐδὲν">nothing  </char>, 
      </group>
      <group indent="1">
        except to be thrown out and stepped on <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="black">by people</char>. 
      </group>
    </group>
  </para>
  <para>
    <group title="Light and City" type="primary">
      <group>
        <verse number="14" /> <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="red">Y’all</char> are <char mark-variant="highlight-dark" mark-color="orange">the light</char> <char mark-variant="text" mark-color="orange">of the world</char>. 
      </group>
      <optbreak />
      <group>
        <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="turquoise" word-lang="greek" word-original="οὐ">It is not  </char> able to be hidden, <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="tan">a city</char> that is set up on a mountain, 
      </group>
      <group>
        <verse number="15" /> and they <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="turquoise" word-lang="greek" word-original="οὐδὲ">don’t  </char> light <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="tan" word-lang="greek" word-original="λύχνον">a candle  </char> and place it under a basket. 
      </group>
      <group>
        Rather, upon a <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="tan" word-lang="greek" word-original="λυχνίαν">candle-stand  </char>, 
      </group>
      <group>
        and it <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="tan">will shine</char> on everyone in the house. 
      </group>
      <optbreak />
      <group>
        <verse number="16" /> In the same way, <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="tan">let</char> <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="red">your</char> <char mark-variant="highlight-dark" mark-color="orange">light</char> <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="tan">shine</char> <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="black">before people</char>, 
      </group>
      <group>
        so that they can see <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="red">your</char> good works, 
      </group>
      <group>
        and so they can give honor to <char mark-variant="highlight" mark-color="red">your</char> Father who is <char mark-variant="highlight-light" mark-color="blue">in the skies</char>
      </group>
    </group>
  </para>
</usx>
